claims.claim_ar: إشارةٌ إلى إعجاز القرآن وإعطاءه صفة الإعجاز كدليل على أصالته وتفوقه على الكتب السابقة.
claims.claim_en: Allusion to the Quran's inimitability (i'jaz): the text presents the Qur'an as miraculous over previous scriptures, serving as measure and proof of their truth.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Strengthens the authority and miraculous status of the Book, giving the opening clause weight as a proof against claims of fabrication.

claims.claim_ar: أسلوب تقريري حكيم: تقديم القرآن هنا كـ "تصديق وتفصيل" لما كان بين يدي الكتاب من الشرائع والبيان، تكثيف حججي وبياني لتأكيد الصلة والشرح.
claims.claim_en: Asloob hakim (wise/authoritative style): the commentary frames the Qur'an as 'confirmation and detailing' of earlier scriptures, a concise argumentative move that asserts its role and authority.
claims.needs_review_reason: Mapping the exegetical phrasing to the discrete K-Maps device label ('asloob_hakim') is interpretive; source is tafsir-explanatory rather than classical rhetorical taxonomy.

claims.claim_ar: توظيف لفظة "تفصيل الكتاب" للدلالة على دور القرآن في التفصيل والبيان، أي صوغ العلاقة بين الكتاب الحالي والكتب السابقة (فصل/وصل بالمضمون).
claims.claim_en: "Tafsil al-kitab" (detailing of the Book): the phrase underscores the Qur'an's function of explaining and detailing what was in prior scriptures, a rhetorical move of separation/connection (fasl/wasl) between previous revelation and this clarification.
claims.needs_review_reason: The assignment of 'fasl_wasl' to this phrase is interpretive; the source states the function (تفصيل) but does not explicitly employ classical 'fasl/wasl' terminology.
